title: Improved and simplified method for aseptic isolation of nematodes and endosymbiotic bacteria
author: Mannaa, Seo
materials: •4-layer pieces (∼4 cm2) of cheesecloth were cut and wrapped in aluminum foil before being placed in an autoclave. They were then sterilized using a standard autoclave cycle at 121 °C for 15 min.•After sterilization, the cheesecloth pieces were transferred into the syringe barrel using sterilized forceps.

steps.title: Sterilize cheesecloth and load into syringe
steps.instruction: Cut ~4 cm² pieces of cheesecloth into four layers, wrap each piece in aluminum foil, autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min, then using sterilized forceps transfer the autoclaved cheesecloth pieces into the barrel of a 50 mL sterile surgical syringe (plunger removed).

steps.title: Extract nematodes from seedling stems
steps.instruction: Using sterile plant‑cutting scissors, cut pine seedlings 2 cm above and below the inoculation cut and harvest a 5–10 cm stem section. Surface‑sterilize the section by immersing it in 70 % ethanol for 2 min, then rinse three times with sterile distilled water (SDW). Cut the sterilized section into ~0.5 cm discs, place the discs onto the autoclaved cheesecloth inside the syringe barrel, re‑insert the plunger and gently compact the tissue. Withdraw 25 mL sterile 10 mM MgSO₄ into the syringe, attach the syringe to a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube, wrap the assembly with plastic wrap, and stand vertically for 8 h in the dark. After 8 h, depress the plunger to release the nematode‑containing solution into the Falcon tube. Then draw a second 25 mL of sterile 10 mM MgSO₄ into the syringe, let it sit for 2 h, and depress the plunger to collect the additional eluate into the same Falcon tube.

steps.title: Pellet and surface‑sterilize nematodes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the nematode suspension at 3000 g for 5 min, discard the supernatant, add 1 % sodium hypochlorite to the pellet and mix gently for 1 min. Wash the pellet three times by resuspending in 10 mM MgSO₄, centrifuging at 3000 g for 5 min each, and discarding the supernatant after each wash.

steps.title: Resuspend, count, and verify sterility
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in an appropriate volume of 10 mM MgSO₄, count the nematodes, and spread 100 µL of the suspension onto a nutrient agar (NA) plate without grinding; incubate briefly to confirm that no bacterial colonies appear, indicating successful surface sterilization.

steps.title: Grind nematodes and plate homogenate
steps.instruction: Under sterile conditions, grind the surface‑sterilized nematodes in a sterile mortar, spread 100 µL of the homogenate onto NA plates, and incubate the plates at 28 °C until bacterial colonies become visible.

steps.title: Select and purify bacterial colonies
steps.instruction: Choose colonies with distinct morphologies and growth rates, sub‑culture each selected colony to obtain pure cultures, and store the purified bacterial cultures under appropriate conditions for future use.

steps.title: Validate nematode isolates
steps.instruction: Examine the isolated nematodes microscopically to confirm their presence and viability; extract DNA from the associated bacterial isolates and perform partial 16S rRNA sequencing to identify the bacterial genera, comparing the results with known nematode‑endosymbiotic bacteria.

description: The protocol detailed herein was employed for the nematode isolation from infected seedling stem tissues (Fig. 3). The obtained nematodes were used for isolation and subsequent identification of bacterial strains that exist as endosymbionts within nematodes. Our surface sterilization of nematodes was confirmed to be effective as plating of unground nematodes on NA plates resulted in no visible bacterial colonies. However, upon grinding surface-sterilized nematodes under aseptic conditions, we isolated several bacterial strains. These strains were identified through partial 16S rRNA sequence analysis and the identified genera (Acinetobacter, Bacillus, Pandoraea, Pantoea, Pseudomonas, Pseudoxanthomonas) are mostly consistent with previous studies on nematode-symbiotic bacteria [3,10,11].Fig. 3Nematode isolation from infected Pinus densiflora seedlings. (A) Photograph of inoculated seedlings. The red circle highlights the region from which samples were cut for nematode isolation. (B) After surface sterilizing the stem cuttings, they were further sectioned into smaller pieces of approximately 0.5 cm. (C) These pieces of stem cutting were placed into the barrel of a 50 mL sterile syringe, which had been pre-filled with multiple layers of autoclaved cheesecloth. (D) 25 mL of sterile 10 mM MgSO4 buffer was then drawn up using the syringe plunger. (E) The syringe was subsequently mounted on top of a Falcon tube and left undisturbed for 8 h at room temperature. This allows the nematodes to be released into the suspension. (F) The plunger is gently pressed to push the solution, along with the nematodes, into the Falcon tube. This solution is then ready for subsequent steps.Fig 3 The validation of our method, was based on specific criteria to assess its effectiveness. Initially, after the isolation process, the extracted nematodes were meticulously examined under a microscope to confirm their presence and evaluate their viability.
